summary: Dartmouth extended need-blind admission to international applicants from the Class of 2026, and meets 100% of demonstrated need for every admitted student with a no-loan policy.
covers: Need-blind admission for all applicants, including international students.
100% of demonstrated need met with grants — no loans.
Families with typical assets earning $125,000 or less: no parent contribution, covering tuition, housing and dining, with an allowance for international travel.
eligibility: First-year applicants from any country applying to Dartmouth College.
Aid is based on demonstrated need, assessed from family income and assets.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Common Application or QuestBridge with Dartmouth's supplement.
Choose binding Early Decision (1 November) or Regular Decision (2 January).
Submit the CSS Profile and Dartmouth's international aid documents by the aid deadline.
Request an application fee waiver if needed.
watch_out: Early Decision is binding — only use it if Dartmouth is your first choice.
Dartmouth's quarter system (the 'D-Plan') is unusual; read how it works before you apply.
Check the current income threshold on Dartmouth's financial aid site; policies have expanded several times since 2022.

faq.q: My school is outside the US. Do I need the SAT or ACT?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Dartmouth accepts the SAT or ACT, three AP exams, or predicted or final results from the IB, British A-levels or an equivalent national exam.

faq.q: Will I have to take out loans?
faq.a: No. Since summer 2022 Dartmouth has removed loans from all undergraduate aid packages. Your need is met with scholarships plus a term-time job.

faq.q: Does my aid follow me if I study abroad?
faq.a: Yes, on Dartmouth's own off-campus programmes. Tuition and your expected family contribution are the same as for a term on campus.
